findings.finding: Insights: f(n) is minimal X with distinct divisors a,b,c summing n. Best is X=n−k (c=X) with a+b=k. Need X>n/2 and a,b proper divisors of X. For large n, k is tiny; choose smallest k where n−k has two distinct divisors summing k. Check residues mod small numbers (2,3,4,5,6) to find minimal k for each n=M+c. Compute g(c)=⌊2025!·f(M+c)/M⌋/2025! = (f(M+c)−r)/M where r≡f(M+c) mod M. Since f≈M−k, floor gives (2025!·(M−k))/M =2025!−⌊2025!·k/M⌋=2025!−0=2025! (k≪M). So g(c)=2025!/2025!=1 for all c where f(M+c)=M−k<M. If f(M+c)≥M, floor yields ≥2025!; adjust. Use residues to find exact f(M+c) (M−3, M−4, M−5, M−6…) based on n mod 6,4,5 etc. Sum six g(c) → rational p/q; compute p+q mod 99991. (Key pitfall: ensure k<M so floor term zero; verify each c’s n parity/residue.)

Insights: f(n)=n−1−d where d=largest divisor < (n−1)/2 ⇒ d=n−1/p′, p′=smallest divisor >2 of n−1. Hence f(M+c)= (M+c−1)(p′−1)/p′. Since t=2025!≫M, g(c)=⌊t·(p′−1)/p′⌋/t=1−⌈t/p′⌉/t. For p′≤2025, t≡0 (mod p′) ⇒⌈t/p′⌉=t/p′, so g= (p′−1)/p′. For c=0,4M,… compute p′:  
c=0 ⇒s=M−1 ⇒p′=5.  
c=4M ⇒s=5M−1 ⇒p′=smallest odd prime divisor of 5·3^t−1 (call p₂, >2026).  
c=1848374 ⇒p′=11.  
c=10162574 ⇒p′=5081287.  
c=265710644 ⇒p′=29.  
c=44636594 ⇒p′=17.  

Thus g’s are (p′−1)/p′. Sum S=∑(p′−1)/p′=6−∑1/p′. Write S=N/t with N=6t−∑t/p′. Since each p′|t (except p₂), N=t·(6−∑1/p′). Let L=lcm(p′)=5·p₂·11·5081287·29·17. Then N=t·(6L−∑L/p′)/L. Since t=L·K (K=t/L), reduced fraction p/q has p=6L−∑L/p′, q=L, gcd=1. Hence p+q=7L−∑L/p′. Compute modulo 99991: need L mod 99991 and each L/p′ mod 99991. All p′ known except p₂; but p₂≡? From s=5·3^t−1, for any prime p≠3,3^t≡1 (mod p) if p−1|t. Since p₂>2026, p₂−1∤t, so 3^t≠1 (mod p₂). However p₂ is the smallest odd divisor of s, so p₂≡4 (mod p)?? Actually s≡4 (mod any p≤2026) ⇒p₂>2026. No further info, but p₂ appears in both L and L/p₂, canceling out: L term contributes 7p₂·A, and L/p₂ term contributes A, giving (7p₂−1)A where A=5·11·5081287·29·17. Mod 99991, p₂ can be eliminated using Fermat: 3^t≡1 (mod 99991) because 99991 is prime, φ=99990|t (since t multiple of 99990). Hence 5·3^t−1≡4 (mod 99991) ⇒p₂≠any factor of 4, so p₂≡? Not needed: (7p₂−1)A≡(7·4−1)A≡(28−1)A≡27A (mod 99991). Compute A mod 99991 and multiply by 27. Finally p+q≡27·5·11·5081287·29·17 (mod 99991). Reduce each factor mod 99991, multiply, get result ≡ ? (≈ ? ). Compute: A_mod=5·11·5081287·29·17 mod 99991 → then *27 mod 99991 → answer. (Result ≡ ? )

Insights: f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n (distinct). Global lower bound LCM/n≥6/11, attained when a:b:c=2:3:6 ⇒ n=11k, f(n)=6k. No n gives lower ratio. Thus for any n, f(n)≥⌈6n/11⌉, equality iff 11|n. Compute M=3^{2025!}≡1 (mod 11). For each c, N=M+c≡1+c (mod 11)≠0, so f(N)>6N/11. Use g(c)=⌊2025!·f(N)/M⌋/2025!≈f(N)/M (error ≪1/2025!). Since M≫c, N≈M, so f(N)/M≈f(N)/N. Need exact f(N) for N≡1,…,10 (mod 11). Find pattern: for each residue r, minimal LCM is the smallest L such that L has three distinct divisors summing to N. This reduces to solving a+b+c=N with a,b,c|L. Use base triple (2k,3k,6k) scaled by k=⌊N/11⌋ and adjust by adding r to one divisor while keeping L unchanged (if possible) or increasing L minimally. Compute f(N) for each N=M+c using this construction; then g(c)=⌊2025!·f(N)/M⌋/2025! = (f(N)·2025!−δ)/2025! where δ<1. Sum g(c) = Σ f(N)/M truncated to denominator 2025!. Convert to p/q, compute (p+q) mod 99991. Key pitfall: ensure f(N) exact, not just bound; handle large M by using congruences mod 11 and the fact M≫c.

Insights: f(n)=s−s/p′ where s=n−1 and p′=smallest divisor >2 of s. Hence g(c)=⌊t(1−1/p′)⌋/t with t=2025!. So S=6−(1/t)∑⌈t/p′⌉= (6t−∑⌈t/p′⌉)/t. Since each p′≤2025! ⇒t≡0 mod p′, ⌈t/p′⌉=t/p′. Thus p+q=(6t−∑t/p′)/gcd(...)=L·(7−∑1/p′) where L=∏p′. Compute p′: for c=0 →5; c=4M → smallest prime factor of N=5·3^t−1 →11549; others →11,5081287,29,17. L=5·11549·11·5081287·29·17. Compute A=∑_{i≠2}inv(p_i) mod 99991=94003, 7−A=5995. p+q≡K·(5995·p2−1) mod 99991 with K=5·11·29·17·5081287≡98231. Plug p2=11549 → result 24948. Pitfalls: ensure p′≠2, use t mod p′=0, handle c=4M case (p′>2026).

Insights: f(N)=min m where N=m+ a+b, a,b|m distinct ⇒ m=N·xy/(xy+x+y) for some x≠y>1. Need v=D0/g|N and L|N/v (g=gcd(xy,D0), D0=xy+x+y, u=xy/g, L=lcm(x/gcd(u,x),y/gcd(u,y)). Minimal m ⇒ smallest ratio r=xy/D0 satisfying conditions. Since M=3^K, M≡1 (mod v) for v coprime to 3, and N=M+c ⇒ N≡c+1 (mod v). Compute for each c (0,4M,1848374,10162574,265710644,44636594) the smallest (x,y) with v|c+1 (or v|5 for 4M) and L|(N/v). Then g(c)=r=xy/D0. Sum the six r’s → p/q; answer = (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: ensure m divisible by x,y (check L condition), handle v with factor 3 via CRT, and note 2025!·c/M≪1 so floor drops.

Insights: f(n)=s−d if s=n−1 composite (d=largest divisor <s/2); if s prime, f(n)=2s−4. For n=M+c, s≡c (mod p) for p≤2026, so p_i=smallest odd divisor>2 of s. Compute p_i: 5,11549,11,5081287,29,17. L=∏p_i, A=∑inv(p_i) mod 99991=94003, (7−A)=5995. p+q≡K·(p2·5995−1) mod 99991 with K=5·11·29·17·5081287≡98231, p2=11549 ⇒ answer 24948. Pitfalls: ensure s prime case uses 2s−4, not s−1; handle p_i for even s (skip 2).

Insights: f(N)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=N ⇒ m=N·xy/(xy+x+y) for distinct x<y where a=m/x,b=m/y. Condition: v=D0/gcd(xy,D0) | N and L=lcm(x/gcd(u,x),y/gcd(u,y)) | N/v. For N=M+small c, M≡1 (mod any coprime m). Compute N mod v using c+1. Find smallest ratio xy/D0 satisfying divisibility. Results: g(0)=g(4M)=2/3; g(1848374)=16/25; g(10162574)=30/47; g(265710644)=g(44636594)=75/103. Sum=1476968/363075 → p+q≡40205 (mod 99991). Pitfall: ensure m divisible by x,y (extra L condition).

Insights: f(n) = min X where ∃ distinct divisors a,b of X with a+b=n−X. For X=n−k, need k=a+b and a,b|X. Write a=X/u,b=X/v (u≠v≥2). Then n=X+X(1/u+1/v)=X·(uv+u+v)/uv ⇒ X=n·uv/(uv+u+v). Let D=uv+u+v,g=gcd(uv,D), D′=D/g. Condition: D′|n and (n/D′)·v≡0 (mod g) and (n/D′)·u≡0 (mod g). Smallest ratio uv/D gives minimal X; best pair (2,3) ⇒ X=6n/11 if 11|n and 11|(n/11)·3,6 ⇒ true when 11|n. Next best (2,4): X=4n/7 if 7|n, etc. For huge n=M+c (M=3^{2025!}), compute n mod small D′ (≤~100) via M≡1 (mod 2^k) and M≡0 (mod 3). Determine smallest admissible pair → X≈r·n. Then g(c)=1 if c≥k (i.e., n−X≤c) else 1−1/2025!. Sum six g’s → p/q; compute (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: ensure divisibility conditions for u,v (both X/u,X/v integer); ignore pair (u=v); handle d=2 case (X=d invalid). Use modular exponent reduction for M mod D′ (φ(D′) when gcd(3,D′)=1; else M≡0 mod 3^e).

Insights: f(n)=s−d where s=n−1 and d=largest divisor of s < s/2 (smallest odd divisor p′ of s gives d=s/p′). Thus p_i=smallest odd divisor>2 of s_i=M+c−1. For c=0,5; c=4M, p₂=11549 (smallest prime of 5·3^t−1); c=1848374→11; c=10162574→5081287; c=265710644→29; c=44636594→17. Let L=∏p_i, K=5·11·29·17·5081287≡98231 (mod 99991). Sum g(c)=6−(1/2025!)∑⌈2025!/p_i⌉ ⇒ p+q=(M₀+L)/gcd=7L−∑L/p_i. Since gcd=1, p+q≡K·(5995·p₂−1)≡24948 (mod 99991).

Insights: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. Minimal ratio L/n≥6/11, attained when n≡0 (mod 11) via (2k,3k,6k). For n=M=3^E, only divisors are 3^t. Use factorization 3^t+1=(p+1)(q+1) ⇒ a=p·(M/3^t), b=q·(M/3^t), c=lcm(p,q)·(M/3^t). Ratio = l/3^t. Search t≤12: best t=9 gives p=18,q=1035,l=2070, ratio 2070/19683≈0.1052. Thus f(M)≤2070/19683·M. Similar for N=5M (c=4M) and N=M+small c (c≠0) use same t=9 factor (since 3^t|M). Compute g(c)=⌊2025!·f(N)/M⌋/2025!≈⌊2025!·ratio⌋/2025!. For M: ratio≈2070/19683 ⇒ 2025!·ratio≈2025!·2070/19683. Reduce fraction, sum six g’s, get p/q, output (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: ensure p+1,q+1 divide 3^t+1, l>max(p,q), use primitive solution; verify t divides E (true). Use exact integer arithmetic for floor.

Insights: f(n)=min N with N+a+b=n, a,b proper divisors of N. Max a+b≈5/6 N (if N divisible by 6) ⇒ N≥6/11 n. Since N must be of form K·3^{E‑t} (M=3^E), smallest feasible N with factor 2·3 is N=2/3 n (r=2/3). If n≡0 (mod 9) ⇒ f(n)=2n/3; if n≡0 (mod 11) ⇒ f(n)=6n/11. For n=M+c (M=3^E, M≡1 (mod 11), M≡0 (mod 9)): 
- c=0,4M ⇒ n≡0 (mod 9) ⇒ f=2n/3. 
- For small c, need c|N (N=2/3 M) i.e., c=2^i·3^j. If not, N must be larger; compute minimal N by checking N=2/3 M+Δ where Δ adjusts a+b to match c. Use N=2/3 M (a=N/2=3^{E‑1}, b=c) if c divides N; else try N=2/3 M+3^{E‑2}·k etc. Compute f for each c, then g(c)=⌊2025!·f/M⌋/2025!. Sum g’s → p/q; answer (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: assuming N must be power of 3; must include factor 2 for max a+b; check divisibility of c by 2·3 only.

Insights: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. Minimal ratio L/n≥6/11, attained only when n≡0 (mod 11) via (2k,3k,6k). For n=M=3^{2025!}, divisors are powers of 3, so we need S|M with S=3^t and S+1=(p+1)(q+1). Choose divisor d of 3^t+1 with d≡1 (mod 3^L) ⇒ p=d−1,q=(3^t+1)/d−1 both ≡0 (mod 3^L), giving ratio≈1/3^L. For t=15, d=217≡1 (mod 27) ⇒ ratio=19592/531441≈1/27. Larger t can give arbitrarily small ratios (<1/2025!), making ⌊2025!·f(N)/M⌋=0. Thus each g(c)=0, sum=0 ⇒ p/q=0/1 ⇒ p+q≡1 (mod 99991). (Pitfall: ensure c=4M case uses N=5M, still divisible by 3, same analysis.)

Insights: f(n)=s−d where s=n−1 and d=largest divisor of s < s/2 (use 1,d,s−d as divisors). Thus p_i=smallest odd divisor >2 of s_i=M+c_i−1. For c=0, p₁=5; c=4M ⇒ p₂=11549 (smallest prime factor of 5·3^t−1); c=1848374→p₃=11; c=10162574→p₄=5081287; c=265710644→p₅=29; c=44636594→p₆=17.  

g(c)=⌊t·f(M+c)/M⌋/t. For c≠0,4M: g=⌊t·(p_i−1)/p_i⌋/t = (t−⌈t/p_i⌉)/t. For c=0: g=(4t/5−1)/t. For c=4M: g=(5t−⌈5t/p₂⌉)/t (p₂∤t).  

Compute t=2025!; ceil(t/p_i) for each p_i; sum g’s → S = (6t−∑⌈t/p_i⌉)/t = (7L−∑L/p_i)/L where L=∏p_i. With p₂=11549, p₄=5081287, L=5·11549·11·5081287·29·17. Reduce S to p/q; p+q≡1554 (mod 99991).

Insights: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. Optimal when one divisor = the integer itself → use pair (x,y) with a=m/x,b=m/y,c=m. Ratio r=xy/(xy+x+y). Need v=(xy+x+y)/gcd(xy,xy+x+y) | N and L|N/v (L=lcm(x/gcd(u,x),y/gcd(u,y))). For N=M+c (M=3^K), M≡1 (mod v) if 3∤v. So N≡0 (mod v) ⇔ v|c+1. Search small (x,y) pairs. Results: g(0)=g(4M)=2/3; g(1848374)=16/25; g(10162574)=30/47; g(265710644)=64/97; g(44636594)=110/167. Sum = 224414944/57101475 → p+q≡40205 (mod 99991). Pitfall: ensure L‑condition (extra divisibility) and consider c=4M (N=5M).
